test_title: RRB Group D Official Paper (Held On: 09 Dec, 2025 Shift 3)
subject: general
question: A train overtakes two people running along a railway track. The first person is running at 12.6 km/hr, and the second person is running at 25.2 km/hr. The train takes 16.8 seconds to pass the first person and 22.4 seconds to pass the second person. What is the speed of the train if both are running in the same direction as the train?
solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Length of train is constant → Relative speed is inversely proportional to time.

Time ratio t₁ : t₂ = 16.8 : 22.4 = 3 : 4.

Relative speed ratio (V − 12.6) : (V − 25.2) = 4 : 3.

3(V − 12.6) = 4(V − 25.2) ⇒ 3V − 37.8 = 4V − 100.8.

V = 100.8 − 37.8 = 63 km/hr.

**∴ Answer = 63 km/hr**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Speed of first person (v₁) = 12.6 km/hr

Speed of second person (v₂) = 25.2 km/hr

Time to pass first person (t₁) = 16.8 s

Time to pass second person (t₂) = 22.4 s

**Formula used:**

Distance = Relative Speed × Time

Relative Speed (Same direction) = Speed of Train (V) − Speed of Person (v)

 TRAIN Speed: V P1: 12.6 km/h P2: 25.2 km/h 
• 
 
• 
 
• 
 Distance = Length of Train (Constant) 

**Calculations:**

Let V be the speed of the train in km/hr.

⇒ Length of train = (V − 12.6) × (16.8 / 3600) = (V − 25.2) × (22.4 / 3600)

⇒ (V − 12.6) × 16.8 = (V − 25.2) × 22.4

⇒ (V − 12.6) / (V − 25.2) = 22.4 / 16.8

⇒ (V − 12.6) / (V − 25.2) = 4 / 3

⇒ 3 × (V − 12.6) = 4 × (V − 25.2)

⇒ 3V − 37.8 = 4V − 100.8

⇒ V = 100.8 − 37.8

⇒ V = 63 km/hr

**∴ The correct answer is (1).**
